chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not upon the one performing Itikaaf that he goes out from the Masjid except to the Friday (Prayer), or a funeral, or defecation.

key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفِ: The one performing Itikaaf (spiritual retreat in the mosque)

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible reasons for a person performing Itikaaf to leave the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the permissible exceptions for breaking the state of Itikaaf, emphasizing that departure is restricted strictly to essential religious duties (Friday prayer, funerals) and biological needs. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle of minimizing distraction to maximize spiritual devotion, distinguishing between obligatory acts that require physical presence in the mosque and those that do not.
